source_text: Σίδηρος οὐκ ἀνέβη ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλήν μου ὅτι Ναζιραῖος τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐγώ εἰμι. Δι᾿ ὅλης τῆς περὶ τὸν Σαμψὼν ἱστορίας αἱ τρίχες φαίνονται τὴν πᾶσαν αὐτῷ περιποιεῖν ἰσχύν.
thought_title: Samson's hair as the source of his strength
orientation: Origen is explaining why Samson says no iron has come upon his head: because he is a Nazirite of God, and throughout the story his hair is shown to secure all his strength.
pass_a_gloss: Iron [has] not gone up upon my head, because [a] Nazirite of God I am. Through [the] whole of the story about Samson the hairs appear to secure for him all [his] strength.

choices.term: Σίδηρος οὐκ ἀνέβη ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλήν μου
choices.english: No iron has come up upon my head
choices.why: Keeps the literal spatial verb 'went up' for the razor's movement onto the head, matching the source's physical image
rejected: No razor has touched my head
Iron has not come upon my head

choices.english: I am a Nazirite of God
choices.why: Preserves the emphatic word order with the predicate first and the pronoun last, as in the source
rejected: a Nazirite of God am I

choices.term: αἱ τρίχες φαίνονται τὴν πᾶσαν αὐτῷ περιποιεῖν ἰσχύν
choices.english: the hairs appear to secure for him all his strength
choices.why: Keeps 'appear' as the main verb and 'secure' as the infinitive, preserving the source's construction and the present tense of the observation
rejected: his hair is shown to be the source of all his strength
the hairs evidently provide him all his strength

choices.why: Renders the verb's sense of acquiring or preserving something for someone, fitting the idea that the hair maintains his strength

bible_refs.note: Σίδηρος οὐκ ἀνέβη ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλήν μου ὅτι Ναζιραῖος τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐγώ εἰμι

pass_b_english: "No iron has come up upon my head, because I am a Nazirite of God" (Judges 16:17). Throughout the whole story of Samson, his hair appears to secure for him all his strength.
